title: Contours & Relief
note: Brand new lesson. practice_data was {} before this run, so nothing was repaired, everything was authored. Repaired 21 Jul after an independent checker found an invented map fact on Worsaw Hill; see problems_fixed and map_facts_verified[7].

Display said 'there is one more, smaller ring' (there are two) and guided_steps[2] asked for that count with answer 1, so a student reading the map correctly was marked wrong. Reworded to 'the next ring in from the labelled line' and the ring-counting box removed; stored solution 210 is unchanged and is now true under the wording given.

opener_concept: A hill built from four flat 10 m slices, seen from the side and then from directly above: the student counts the slices (40 m) and the rings (4), and the reveal names the rings as contour lines.
map_facts_verified: Contour interval is 10 m on every extract: on snowdonia-z15 exactly 4 thin lines lie between the thick lines labelled 650 and 700 (pixel scan at y=650 found brown runs at x=884 thick, 903, 921, 939, 958, 978 thick; confirmed visually at 9x zoom). Independently reconfirmed on pendle-hill-z16 where a vertical scan at x=1330 found the labelled 200 index at y=289, four thin lines at y=319/334/350/362, then the next index at y=374 (= 150 m).

Grid line pixel positions measured by blue-line detection. yorkshire-dales-z15: eastings 88/89/90/91 at x=279/636/994/1351, northings 74/73/72 at y=286/643/999 (357 px per km). pendle-hill-z16: eastings 76/77/78 at x=43/754/1466, northings 43/42 at y=433/1140. lake-district-z16: eastings 34/35/36 at x=56/784/1512, northings 09/08 at y=345/1053. snowdonia-z15: eastings 67 to 71 at x=16/372/728/1084/1440.

Cow Close Fell (yorkshire-dales-z15): thick index contour labelled 600 at approx (483,790); two thin rings nested inside it, so the innermost ring is 620 m; the innermost ring spans x 370-500, y 665-780, entirely inside grid square 8872.

Grid square 9073 (yorkshire-dales-z15, x 994-1351, y 286-643) contains zero contour lines: six horizontal pixel scans at y=320/380/440/500/560/620 all returned count 0. Neighbouring square 8973 returned 4 to 12 crossings per scan.
Litton village and the River Skirfare sit on the flat floor of Littondale in that same part of the sheet (label positions read at 3x zoom).

The contour labelled 550 on the western flank of Cow Close Fell (thick line at x=68 to 85, y=762, label printed at approx (75,752)) and the 600 ring (thick line at x=247, same row) are 171 px apart, which at 357 px per km is 0.48 km, quoted in the lesson as about 0.5 km. Rise 50 m over 0.5 km gives 100 m per km, or 1 in 10.
Yorkshire sheet also prints contour labels 400 (north-west quarter, approx (318,258), with northing line 74 immediately below it), 450 and 500 near Darnbrook Fell.

CORRECTED 21 Jul after checker challenge. Worsaw Hill (pendle-hill-z16): thick index contour labelled 200 at approx (1440,168). TWO closed rings are drawn inside it, not one. Vertical pixel scan at x=1377 returns brown runs at y=23-24 (index, 200 N), y=60-61 (thin, 210 N), y=165-167 and y=174-176 (the two limbs of a small closed loop, 220), y=287 (thin, 210 S), y=317 (index, 200 S). The small loop was re-imaged at 16x: it is a closed ring about 3 px wide and 12 px tall spanning x 1376-1379, y 165-176, in thin-contour brown (145,118,97) against the thin-contour reference and clearly not an index line (index runs on this sheet read approx (135,90,55)). So the highest ring drawn is 220 m and the first undrawn contour is 230 m. Independently consistent with Worsaw Hill's real summit height of 228 m. The original entry claiming 'exactly one thin ring inside' was WRONG and had cleared two defective problems (gold[4], bronze[1]); both have been rewritten.

Worsaw Hill southern slope is far steeper than its northern slope: south, 200 m down to the 150 m index in 85 px (0.12 km); north at x=1250, the 200 index at y=222 with the next line not until y=27 (0.27 km for one step).

Greenhead Gill (lake-district-z16, label at approx (720,670), grid square 3408): stream drawn in blue flowing south-west, contours bending into sharp points aimed north-east, i.e. upstream. Verified on a 3x crop of x 500-1000, y 520-820.
Stone Arthur (lake-district-z16, label at approx (680,165), north of the 09 northing line at y=345): contours swing out into rounded points facing south-west towards Grasmere, i.e. a spur.
Lake district eastern side prints index labels 600 (1287,255), 550 (1290,858), 500 (1394,1011), 450 (1394,1178); contours in square 3508 east of Heron Pike are packed almost touching.

Worsaw Hill north slope re-verified for silver[4]: at x=1250 the only brown runs between y=0 and y=320 are y=219-222 and y=26-27, i.e. one interval crossed in about 193 px (0.27 km). On the south at x=1330 the 200 index at y=289-292 is followed by the next line at y=319, 30 px (0.04 km). The southern side is far steeper, as silver[4] states.

silver[6] re-verified: vertical scan at x=1330 south of the summit gives index 200 at y=289-292, four thin lines at y=319/334/350/362, then the next index at y=374-375, so the lower thick line is 150 m.

checker_findings_rejected.finding: silver[3].guided_steps[1].answer stored as 9 while the map prints '09'; a string compare would fail a correct student.
checker_findings_rejected.reason: Not a defect. practice.html line 5571 checks guided boxes with parseFloat((input.value||'').trim()) and Math.abs(v - st.answer) < 0.005. There is no string compare anywhere in the guided-step path, so a student typing 09 parses to 9 and is marked right. The spec also requires guided-step answers to be plain numbers, and 09 is not a valid JSON number. Left as 9. The only residual is cosmetic: after a second wrong attempt the reveal writes String(9) = '9' rather than '09'.
